speaker: Doctor
text: How would you describe the onset and location of your wrist pain, and does it radiate into your fingers or forearm?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the radiation to the elbow and your mother's history of rheumatoid arthritis are concerning. Given the trauma six months ago, was there any specific injury or fracture identified at that time, and do you notice morning stiffness in your hands that lasts more than 30 minutes? REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP, RF, and Anti-CCP.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since your inflammatory markers are normal, this makes a systemic autoimmune cause less likely. Does the pain specifically worsen when you extend your thumb against resistance, and do you have any numbness or tingling in your thumb, index, or middle fingers?

REQUEST TEST: Nerve_Conduction_Study; REQUEST IMAGES: Right_wrist_XRay

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Nerve Conduction Study: Normal sensory and motor conduction velocities with no evidence of focal neuropathy or entrapment. Right Wrist X-ray: No fracture, dislocation, or degenerative changes. Soft tissue swelling noted over the radial styloid.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal nerve conduction study and X-ray effectively rule out carpal tunnel syndrome, fractures, and advanced arthritis, but the soft tissue swelling over the radial styloid combined with pain on thumb extension is highly suspicious for De Quervain's tenosynovitis. Does the pain significantly worsen when you simultaneously make a fist, extend your wrist, and tilt your palm away from you (Finkelstein's maneuver)?

REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound of Right Wrist; DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis
